problem: writeExportFile swallows any mkdir/writeFile failure (it only logs, and only when KERYX_VERBOSE is set) and returns normally. runHistoryExport then proceeds as if the write succeeded: line 131 prints 'exported N run(s) to <file>' and exitCode stays 0. Error-handling Rule 3 / Iron Law 1: a catch that hides a failure from a caller who then proceeds is forbidden. This is the only call site.
impact: A user exporting to an unwritable or invalid path (read-only dir, path under an existing file, full disk) is told the export succeeded and gets exit 0; scripts and flow journals that attach the file find it missing or stale. Fix: let the error propagate (or rethrow with the target path and cause) and set exitCode 1.

problem: The doc comment on collectRunRows claims it 'Returns the runs oldest first, so the exported file reads in the order the writes happened', but the body only filters the result of listWikiRuns, which is documented and implemented as 'Runs newest first' (src/wiki/history.ts:495, :508). The comment asserts an ordering the code does not produce.
impact: Readers and callers of the exported collectRunRows trust an order that is the reverse of the real one; either the comment or the code is wrong, and the next maintainer cannot tell which was intended.
quote: oldest first, so the exported file reads in the order the writes happened.

problem: The command-label normalization chain (collapse CR/LF, collapse whitespace, trim, slice to MAX_COMMAND_WIDTH) is copied three times: wiki-history-export.ts:49-53 (markdown branch), wiki-history-export.ts:56-60 (CSV branch), and wiki-history.ts:47-51 (terminal listing). Only MAX_COMMAND_WIDTH was shared; the transform itself was not extracted.
impact: Any change to how labels are clipped or sanitized must be made in three places; a missed copy makes the terminal list and the exported file disagree on the same run.

problem: renderRunLine takes a boolean flag `markdown` that selects between two different renderers (markdown row vs CSV row), and 4 positional parameters, two of which (`at`, `pages`) are derived from `run` itself. The call site reads renderRunLine(run, at, run.pages, format === "md") (line 119).
impact: Call sites are opaque and the signature invites passing values inconsistent with `run`; adding a third format means another branch inside the flag. Two functions (renderCsvRow/renderMarkdownRow) or a format-keyed map taking just the run would remove both problems.
quote: export function renderRunLine(run: WikiRunSummary, at: string, pages: number, markdown: boolean): string {

problem: runHistoryExport is ~57 lines and does several separable jobs at mixed levels: option parsing/validation (--export, --format with extension inference, --since date parsing), row rendering (lines 116-120, a pure transform), file I/O (line 122), and display-path resolution (lines 124-130). The rendering transform sits inline in the I/O shell instead of a pure helper.
impact: The option parsing and the body rendering cannot be tested without touching the filesystem and process.exitCode; extending the command means growing one long function.

problem: The catch rethrows a new Error without `cause` (the caught `error` binding is unused) and the message does not name the input (cwd / runs-log path). Error-handling Rule 5 and Iron Law 3.
impact: The real reason (permission denied, corrupt file, which path) is discarded; whoever debugs a failed export sees only a generic message.
quote: throw new Error("wiki history: could not read the runs log");

problem: The same new option set is documented three different ways: HISTORY_USAGE lists only '[--export <file> [--format csv|md]]', while EXPORT_USAGE (wiki-history-export.ts:13) and the wiki help text (wiki.ts:924) also list --since and --command. Two places document one behaviour inconsistently.
impact: Users reading the history usage line do not learn that --since/--command exist; the three strings will keep drifting since none derives from another.
